chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Sayf, from one of our companions, from Abu Ja‘far al-Thani عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him عليه السلام: “They are speaking about the youth of your age.”

So he عليه السلام said: “Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, revealed to Dawud that he should appoint Sulayman as the khalifah, while he was a young boy tending sheep. So the worshippers of the Children of Israel and their scholars objected to that. Then Allah revealed to Dawud عليه السلام: ‘Take the staffs of those speaking and the staff of Sulayman, and place them in a house, and seal them with the seals of the people. Then when the next day comes, whichever staff has put forth leaves and borne fruit, he is the khalifah.’”
So Dawud informed them, and they said: “We are satisfied, and we submit.”
ai.seo_question: How does this hadith answer objections to the young age of an Imam?
ai.summary: This narration addresses the objection to the young age of the Imam by drawing a parallel with the appointment of Sulayman by Dawud عليهما السلام while Sulayman was still a boy. It emphasizes that divine appointment is based on Allah’s choice, and that Allah may manifest signs to confirm the legitimacy of His chosen khalifah.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Sayf, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> the 2<sup>nd</sup>, said, ‘
I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘They (people) are talking regarding the infancy of your<sup>asws</sup> age’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted Revealed unto Dawood<sup>as</sup> that he<sup>as</sup> choose Suleyman<sup>as</sup> as the Caliph, and he<sup>as</sup> was a child pasturing sheep. So the worshippers of the Children of Israel and their scholars denied that. So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Revealed unto Dawood<sup>as</sup>: “Take the staffs of the speakers and the staff of Suleyman<sup>as</sup> and make these to be in a house, and seal upon these with the seals of the people. So when it would be the morning, the one whose staff would have sprouted leaves and fruit, so he<sup>asws</sup> would be the Caliph”.
So Dawood<sup>as</sup> informed them, and they said, ‘We agree and submit’’.
en.sarwar: 3. mmd ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Sayf from certain persons of our people from abu Ja‘far (a.s.) al-Thani (the second).
The narrator has said that I said to him “They speak about (and question) your very young age.

He said, “Allah informed David through inspiration to appoint Sulayman as the executor of his will and successor while he was just a child minding sheep. The worshippers and scholars of the Israelites disliked it. Allah then inspired David to take the staff of those who have objections and that of Sulayman and place them in a room and seal them with each one’s seals. On the next day whichever staff would be found that has grown leaves and fruits the owner thereof would be the successor.
David informed them of this matter and they all agreed.”
